title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + ROPE fused ops + KV-batching + scheduler tweaks
author: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: This PR upgrades the attention execution path to FlashAttentionV2-derived kernels with optimizations for ROPE/rotary encodings, introduces a small set of fused-op kernels for QKV+apply_rotary and softmax+dropout fusion, and adds conservative KV-cache-aware continuous-batching and scheduler heuristics. Motivation: long-context workloads and multi-tenant Dedicated deployments show disproportionate tail latency and GPU memory overhead when many small cached requests are mixed with large sequence generations. Goals were: 1) reduce per-token latency for long sequences, 2) reduce tail latency for mixed-size workloads, 3) reduce peak GPU memory for KV cache copies, and 4) maintain numerical parity within tolerance for model correctness. What changed: - Replaced existing attention kernels with FlashAttnV2-compatible kernels on supported GPUs (CUDA>=12, sm>=80), falling back to previous kernels for older hardware. - Added ROPE/rotary fused ops to apply rotary embeddings as part of QKV gather to reduce memory traffic. - Implemented fused softmax+dropout where applicable to reduce kernel launches. - KV-cache batching: group KV cache updates for small, concurrent requests to amortize kernel overhead. - Scheduler heuristics: detect high contention patterns and prefer batching window expansion for small requests; add conservative backoff on batching window for long-request dominated queues. - Added feature flag runtime.enable_flashattnv2 and runtime.kv_batching.enabled to gate on rollout. Benchmarks: - Long sequence (8k tokens) throughput improved ~1.9x and p50 latency reduced ~18% on A100-80GB. - Mixed workload (many 32-token requests + occasional 2k requests) tail p99 latency reduced ~28% after KV batching + scheduler tweaks. - Peak GPU memory for KV cache reduced ~12% due to fused ROPE and more efficient staging. Compatibility & fallbacks: - Auto-detects unsupported devices and falls back to existing kernels. - Numeric differences were verified against gold model outputs on a suite of 120 prompts (mean L2 diff < 1e-6, max diff within expected FP16 variance). Rollout plan: - Feature-flagged rollout: enable in internal perf lab -> gradual rollout to canary Dedicated pools -> broad rollout in 2 weeks pending SLO checks. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests with kv-cache scenarios - [x] Microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf harness runs attached - [x] Feature flags and metrics emitted - [x] Documentation update (runtime flags + compatibility notes) - [x] Migration/fallback tests (old GPUs) Testing performed: - CI: unit + integration on CUDA 12 runners, synthetic perf harness across sequence lengths. - Perf lab: A100 and H100 runs, multi-tenant isolated runs and mixed-workload stress tests. - Evals: correctness suite + smoke tests against downstream APIs. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: numeric divergence for some models; mitigation: gated feature flag and conservative rollout. - Risk: increased kernel code complexity; mitigation: added extensive unit tests and perf regression alerts. Related linear/JIRA: ENG-1245, ENG-1302, SUP-872. More details: see the commit list and the changed files below for exact changes to the runtime kernel registration, scheduler, and the kv cache staging path.
